name_note: GTDB splits the classical species Faecalibacterium prausnitzii into several species-level lineages, of which F. prausnitzii_E is one, so published work on F. prausnitzii covers a broader group.

sentences.text: It is described as a member of clostridial cluster IV that produces butyrate, a metabolite reported to be the preferred energy source of colon epithelial cells.

A review describes butyrate production by this species as arising partly from cross-feeding interactions with bifidobacteria stimulated by prebiotics such as inulin-type fructans and arabinoxylan-oligosaccharides.
A study reported it to be underrepresented in patients with COVID-19, and an inverse correlation has been reported between its abundance and disease severity.
